title: Online Medical Supply and Equipment
desc: Run an honest online shop for medical supplies and equipment: sourcing, rules, product information, storage and safe delivery.
outcomes: Explain which supplies are general goods and which are regulated devices.
Write accurate product pages with warnings, storage and returns.
Check suppliers for licence, batch records and cold or dry storage needs.
Judge risks in a product line and decide what you will not sell.
Launch a small catalogue with order-to-delivery steps.
task: Plan and open a small online catalogue of 10 low-risk supplies with verified suppliers, product pages, storage rules and a recall plan.
condition: A spreadsheet, a basic shop tool, supplier documents (real or practice), two peers and a mentor with trade knowledge. Rules are checked with an adviser.
standard: Every product has a licence or rule check; no medical claims beyond the label; storage and expiry rules are written; recall plan runs in a mock test in under 24 hours; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Small traders, pharmacy and clinic staff, logistics staff and entrepreneurs entering health retail.
evidence: product register, supplier checks, 10 product pages, storage plan, recall test record
modules: What can you sell, and who may
Understand
Health products sit on a risk ladder. Selling the wrong item can hurt people.
General items: gloves, masks, thermometers (check rules), bandages. Regulated: prescription medicines, many devices; these need a licence and sometimes a pharmacist.
Check the rule in your place before listing: licence, registration, age limits, prescription need.
Start with low-risk items and grow only with a licensed partner.
A trader lists blood pressure monitors only after learning that her country needs a device registration; she waits for a licensed distributor.
List 20 items and sort them into low risk, needs licence, do not sell.
Each item has a rule note with a source.
Supplier checks
Analyse
A shop is only as safe as its supplier.
Ask for licence, batch number, expiry date, storage needs and a product data sheet.
Test with a small order; inspect packs, labels and seals.
Keep records for each batch so you can trace and recall.
A glove supplier cannot give batch numbers; the trader drops the offer and picks one with labelled cartons.
Complete a supplier check form for two suppliers.
Forms are filled with real or practice evidence; one supplier is rejected with a reason.
Product pages that tell the truth
Create
Pages must be clear, accurate and not claim to cure.
State what it is, size, quantity, intended use, warnings, storage and expiry.
Use only the maker's approved claims; never promise cures or diagnosis.
Show real photos and a clear return rule.
Weak: "Best protection against disease." Strong: "Single-use nitrile gloves, size M, box of 100, not for sterile surgery."
Write 10 product pages.
Pages have all required facts; no unapproved claim.
Storage, cold chain and expiry
Apply
Heat, damp and age spoil supplies.
Store dry, clean, off the floor, away from sunlight and pests; track temperature if needed.
First-expiry-first-out: sell earliest expiry first; remove expired stock to a labelled bin.
Record temperature or humidity checks on a daily log.
A strip of test kits needs 2 to 8 degrees; a fridge log is kept twice a day and a spoiled batch is separated.
Draw a storage plan and daily log sheet.
Plan covers heat, damp, expiry and pest control.
Orders, packing and delivery
Apply
Right item, right condition, right person.
Check each order against the pick list; seal and label; protect from shock and heat.
Choose a courier able to handle the product; give tracking.
Verify age or prescription where the rule needs it.
An order of ear drops is held until the prescription is checked by the partner pharmacist.
Write the order-to-delivery steps and run a mock order.
Mock order passes with no mistakes.
Returns, complaints and recall
Evaluate
Plan for failure before it happens.
Medical items usually cannot be resold after opening; write a clear returns rule.
A recall plan: find batch, stop sales, tell buyers, collect stock, report to the authority, record.
Log every complaint and look for patterns.
A batch of masks has a seal fault. The shop finds 40 buyers by batch number within 6 hours.
Run a mock recall within 24 hours.
Every step is recorded with time.
Privacy and payment safety
Evaluate
Order data can reveal health, which is sensitive.
Collect only what is needed; store securely; delete when no longer needed.
Use payment methods approved in your place; never ask for card numbers by message.
Pack discreetly where the product is private.
The shop removes the product name from the delivery label and shows only the order number.
Write a one-page privacy and payment note.
Note lists data kept, why, and for how long.
Launch and improve
Create
Open small, learn, and grow only what is safe.
Launch with 10 items; track orders, complaints, returns and stock-outs.
Review monthly with a licensed adviser; add items only after the rule check.
Plan responsible disposal and give customer safety tips.
After one month: 62 orders, 2 complaints, 0 recalls; one item removed for slow sales and a supplier changed.
Present your launch review.
Numbers are true and a clear next step is dated.
quiz: Name one low-risk and one regulated item.
Bandages low risk; prescription medicine or a regulated device regulated.
What must a supplier provide?
Licence, batch number, expiry date, storage needs, data sheet.
Why avoid cure claims?
They mislead buyers and are usually illegal.
What does first-expiry-first-out mean?
Sell the earliest-expiry stock first.
Why keep batch records?
To trace and recall products fast.
What is a returns rule for opened medical items?
Usually not resellable; state it clearly.
Name two storage dangers.
Heat and damp (also pests, sunlight).
What should delivery labels avoid?
Showing private product names.
When do you add a new product?
After the rule check with a licensed adviser.
How long should a mock recall take here?
Under 24 hours.

Forms plus test order and batch records
Each supplier's licence number and date recorded
Licence checks dated, and one sample batch traced from supplier to shelf
Risk class of each item unknown
